_meta.indication: Add-on therapy to ravulizumab or eculizumab for treatment of extravascular hemolysis (EVH) in adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH).

pivotal_trials.design: Multiregional, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled study of danicopan versus placebo as add-on to ravulizumab or eculizumab.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with PNH and clinically evident EVH (hemoglobin ≤ 9.5 g/dL and ARC ≥ 120 ×10^12/L) treated with a stable dose of eculizumab or ravulizumab for at least 6 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change in hemoglobin relative to baseline after 12 weeks of danicopan compared to placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: N=86 randomized (42 VOYDEYA, 21 placebo in interim analysis set; safety population 57 VOYDEYA and 29 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in Hgb from baseline to Week 12: 2.9 g/dL (VOYDEYA) vs 0.5 g/dL (placebo); treatment difference 2.4 g/dL (95% CI 1.7, 3.2); P=0.0007. Hgb increase ≥2 g/dL in absence of transfusion: 59.5% vs 0%. Transfusion avoidance: 83.3% vs 38.1%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (≥10%) was headache (11% vs 10% placebo). Other reactions ≥5%: vomiting (7%), pyrexia (7%), ALT increased (5%), hypertension (5%). Serious adverse reactions in 5% of subjects included pancreatitis and cholecystitis. Warnings include serious encapsulated bacterial infections, hepatic enzyme increases, and hyperlipidemia.
target_moa: Oral complement inhibitor that targets factor D to reversibly inhibit the complement alternative pathway, inhibiting AP-mediated hemolysis and preferentially controlling C3 fragment-mediated extravascular hemolysis.
modality: small molecule (oral factor D complement inhibitor)

boxed_warning.content: Serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria (Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae type B), which may become rapidly life-threatening or fatal; vaccination required and available only through the VOYDEYA REMS.

rems.type: VOYDEYA REMS — a restricted program with elements to assure safe use because of the risk of serious infections caused by encapsulated bacteria; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened; no issues were identified that would have benefited from public discussion with external experts.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA for danicopan (VOYDEYA), which held orphan drug designation for PNH and Breakthrough Therapy Designation; approved as add-on to ravulizumab or eculizumab for EVH in adults with PNH based on Study ALXN2040-PNH-301, with a boxed warning and REMS for serious encapsulated bacterial infections.

requirement.text: 4601-1 Establish a registry to characterize the long-term safety of danicopan in adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), with at least 5 years of follow-up. Yearly safety follow-up data should include a summary of the major safety findings for all patients and all serious infections with encapsulated bacteria. The final study report should include an integrated safety dataset and patient level data, including data on danicopan dosing, meningococcal and pneumococcal vaccination status, and concomitant medications.
